GAHT plasma proteomics analysis results

Phenotype comparison: Plasma proteins altered after 6 months of feminizing GAHT, CPA vs SPIRO antiandrogen regimens.

Key findings:
- CPA (n=20): 95 proteins significantly altered (36 up, 59 down)
- SPIRO (n=20): 23 proteins significantly altered (5 up, 18 down)
- CPA vs SPIRO: 9 proteins with significantly different fold-changes
- Shared core GAHT signature: 10 proteins concordantly changed in both regimens
- CPA induces a stronger proteomic shift than SPIRO, consistent with its dual antiandrogen+progestin pharmacology

Top CPA changes: INSL3 −5.22 (adj.P=5.7e-12, Leydig cell marker), SPINT3 −7.78, EDDM3B −2.54 (testis/epididymis proteins), PRL +1.51 (prolactin, estrogenic), LEP +1.62 (leptin), CXCL13 +1.97 (immune)

Top SPIRO changes: PROK1 −0.75, SPINT3 −3.40, LEP +1.17 (all shared with CPA but attenuated)

Differential (CPA vs SPIRO): INSL3 more down in CPA (−3.59, adj.P=5.0e-06 — key discriminator), PRL more up (+1.19), SPINT3 more down (−4.39), REN more down (−0.75)

Conclusion: CPA and SPIRO share a core estrogen-driven proteomic signature, but CPA produces substantially stronger suppression of testis-specific proteins (especially INSL3), reflecting its central gonadotropin suppression via progestin activity that SPIRO lacks.

Output files: outputs/3b81d3cf-b4b9-4a2b-8ea2-3630207f9377/CPA_6months_vs_baseline_DE.csv, SPIRO_6months_vs_baseline_DE.csv, CPA_vs_SPIRO_diff_DE.csv, gaht_proteomics_analysis.h5ad, figures/
